source.title: MDMLP: Image Classification from Scratch on Small Datasets with MLP
source.authors: Tian-Xu Lv; Chong-Yang Bai; Chao-Jie Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study compares image-classification accuracy of MLP-family models and a convolutional ResNet, with mixed results across datasets that qualify the convolutional advantage. It does not test the mechanism of local connectivity.
record.gate_note: The reported table accuracies are held-out classification results. The paper does not report training error or a train–test gap. It states that all models used horizontal flip and color jitter, SGD, weight decay 0.0001, batch size 128 (16 for Flowers102), 200 epochs, cosine learning-rate decay, and warm-up 10. No results isolate the effects of these training choices.
record.test_reason: The study compares ResNet20 with structured, patch-based MLP architectures and a Transformer, rather than the fully connected image networks named in V3. An MLP-family designation does not establish that equivalence: these architectures mix selected dimensions and share parameters, and MDMLP explicitly uses convolution-equivalent overlapping patch embeddings. The only explicitly identified fully connected baseline, S-FC, is taken from another paper. No own results test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that MDMLP enables competitive training from scratch on small image datasets with substantially fewer parameters than existing MLP models, and that MDAttnTool visualizes learned features. They acknowledge disappointing throughput relative to FLOPS and failure to outperform state of the art on every dataset. Their assertion of superiority on all three metrics on Flowers102 and Food101 is inconsistent with Table 2: ResNet20 has fewer parameters.
record.recipe_differences: Architecture comparison on small image datasets with SGD and light augmentation; no training-error or generalization-gap analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and MLP architecture change which model has higher reported accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet20 outperforms most structured MLP models, but ViP exceeds it on CIFAR-100 and MDMLP exceeds it on Flowers102 and Food101; AS-MLP essentially ties it on Food101.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under this 200-epoch SGD recipe, the accuracy ordering between ResNet20 and structured patch-based MLP architectures depends on dataset and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet20 outperforms ViT on all four datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: This ResNet20 configuration achieves higher held-out accuracy than the tested ViT configuration when both are trained from scratch under the reported recipe.

record.problems: No training accuracy or train–test gap is reported; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Comparisons include some results taken from corresponding papers, and the study does not isolate local connectivity as a mechanism.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Own comparisons with fully connected image networks; learned sparse local connections; convolutional initialization; the causal contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning dependence.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout ablations, small-data dependence, and augmentation or weight-decay interactions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with measured generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All reported accuracies are retained as numerical results, but cannot determine the named versions. MLP-family membership should not be conflated with an ordinary fully connected image architecture. Independently, the extraction's blanket reversed states are directionally wrong wherever the CNN scores higher: those differences favor a convolutional advantage. No uncertainty or training-error measurements are reported. Table 3's architectural ablations concern overlapping patches and MDBlocks, not any named version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization for the same model and recipe.
A width sweep beyond interpolation and resulting test error.

Fully connected networks with learned sparse local connections; convolutional initialization of a fully connected network; local connectivity as a causal mechanism; MNIST and SVHN; training-from-scratch comparisons beyond the reported datasets.
Large- versus small-batch training and recipe adaptations.
Dropout ablations and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other measures of the generalization gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work discuss the accuracy disadvantage of MLPs relative to convolutional networks, but the study's own structured architectures do not establish the fully connected comparison specified by V3.

tranche.reason: The study compares structured patch-based MLP architectures, a Transformer and ResNet20. Its own experiments do not supply V3's fully connected image-network comparison or test another claim version. The S-FC result is taken from reference [14].

source_check.notes: R17 is secondary evidence from reference [14]. Table 2 contradicts the prose's blanket superiority claim across all three metrics: ResNet20 has fewer parameters, and several comparators have lower FLOPS than MDMLP.
